overview.h1: HTS Chapter 29: Organic Chemicals — Tariff Rates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 29 Organic Chemicals Tariff Rates — HS Code 29 Import Duties, APIs, Section 232 & 301 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 1,227 HTS Chapter 29 organic chemical lines — hydrocarbons, alcohols, acids, amines, heterocyclics, vitamins, hormones, antibiotics and drug APIs. Base rates Free to 6.5%, the Pharmaceutical Appendix, Section 232 pharma, Section 301 and China duties.

overview.intro:
Chapter 29 covers separately defined organic chemicals: hydrocarbons and their halogenated or nitrated derivatives (2901–2904); alcohols, phenols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids (2905–2918); esters, amines, amides and other nitrogen compounds (2919–2929); organo-sulfur, organo-inorganic and heterocyclic compounds, where most drug active ingredients sit (2930–2935); and vitamins, hormones, glycosides, alkaloids, pure sugars and antibiotics (2936–2942). It has **1,227 tariff lines**: 307 are Free and 920 carry a base duty, most often 6.5% (401 lines), 3.7% (190 lines), 5.5% (185 lines). The U.S. imported **$103.86B** of these chemicals in 2025, $65.56B of it from Ireland — $56.30B of that in hormones (2937).

Two schedule rules can remove the base rate for any column-1 country: the **Pharmaceutical Appendix** ("Free (K)", 492 lines) for listed drug ingredients and the **intermediate chemicals for dyes** appendix ("Free (L)", 131 lines). The extra duties sit on top: the **2026 Section 301 tariffs** on 60 economies (10% or 12.5%) reach 1,139 lines — only 88 (vitamins, hormones, alkaloids, antibiotics and a few others) are exempt outright, and 702 more are exempt only when the chemical is for use in pharmaceutical applications (9903.05.89). Goods of **China** also pay the older Section 301 lists (25% on 781 lines, 7.5% on 43), goods of **Brazil** a further 25%, and patented drug ingredients on 72 lines the **Section 232 pharmaceutical duty** (100%; 15% for the EU, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland; 0% for the UK; nothing for generics). Canadian mannitol, sorbitol, glycerol and D-arabinose pay a 50% Section 338 duty, and Russian goods pay a 35% rate on 128 lines.

Not in the table: **antidumping and countervailing duties** on more than 25 chemicals (citric acid, glycine, MSG, melamine, HFC refrigerants, vanillin, erythritol and others), the **Superfund excise tax** on imported benzene, toluene, xylene, ethylene, propylene and other taxable chemicals ($9.74 a ton), the ozone-depleting-chemical tax, and the entry rules of DEA (listed precursors and controlled substances), EPA (TSCA, HFC allowances) and FDA (drug ingredients).

productGroups.label: Acyclic hydrocarbons
productGroups.blurb: 13 lines, all Free. Ethylene, propylene, butane, butylene, butadiene and acetylene are also taxable chemicals for the Superfund excise tax ($9.74 a ton).

productGroups.label: Cyclic hydrocarbons (benzene, toluene, xylene, styrene)
productGroups.blurb: 19 lines, all Free. Benzene, toluene and the xylenes are taxable chemicals for the Superfund excise tax ($9.74 a ton); toluene is also a DEA List II chemical.

productGroups.label: Halogenated hydrocarbons (HFCs, HCFCs, CFCs, chlorinated solvents)
productGroups.blurb: 76 lines: 8 Free, 68 dutiable (most at 3.7%); 35 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. HFC refrigerants need EPA allowances under the AIM Act, CFCs, HCFCs and halons fall under the ozone rules and ozone-depleting-chemical tax, and R-134a, R-125 and R-32 from China carry antidumping duties.

productGroups.label: Sulfonated, nitrated or nitrosated hydrocarbons
productGroups.blurb: 31 lines: 1 Free, 30 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 4 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Nitroethane is a DEA List I chemical.

productGroups.label: Acyclic alcohols (methanol, glycols, glycerol, sorbitol)
productGroups.blurb: 44 lines: 6 Free, 38 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 13 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Mannitol, sorbitol and glycerol from Canada pay the 50% Section 338 duty, and erythritol from China carries antidumping and countervailing duties.

productGroups.label: Cyclic alcohols (menthol, benzyl alcohol)
productGroups.blurb: 12 lines: 3 Free, 9 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 3 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Phenols
productGroups.blurb: 20 lines: 3 Free, 17 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 5 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Halogenated or nitrated phenols
productGroups.blurb: 21 lines: 2 Free, 19 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 6 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Ethers, ether-alcohols and peroxides
productGroups.blurb: 33 lines: 4 Free, 29 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 14 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Ethyl ether is a DEA List II chemical.

productGroups.label: Epoxides (ethylene oxide, propylene oxide)
productGroups.blurb: 8 lines: 0 Free, 8 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 6 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Acetals and hemiacetals
productGroups.blurb: 2 lines: 1 Free, 1 dutiable (most at 5.3%); 1 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Aldehydes (formaldehyde, vanillin)
productGroups.blurb: 24 lines: 3 Free, 21 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 4 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Vanillin from China carries antidumping and countervailing duties; benzaldehyde is a DEA List I chemical.

productGroups.label: Halogenated or nitrated aldehydes
productGroups.blurb: 3 lines: 1 Free, 2 dutiable (most at 5.5%).

productGroups.label: Ketones and quinones (acetone, MEK, camphor)
productGroups.blurb: 35 lines: 9 Free, 26 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 14 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Acetone from Belgium, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea and Spain carries antidumping duties; acetone, MEK and MIBK are DEA List II chemicals.

productGroups.label: Saturated monocarboxylic acids (acetic, formic, stearic)
productGroups.blurb: 47 lines: 2 Free, 45 dutiable (most at 5.5%); 23 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Acetic anhydride is a DEA List II and propionic anhydride a List I chemical.

productGroups.label: Unsaturated and aromatic monocarboxylic acids (acrylic, benzoic)
productGroups.blurb: 45 lines: 6 Free, 39 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 8 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Phenylacetic acid is a DEA List I chemical.

productGroups.label: Polycarboxylic acids (adipic, phthalic, terephthalic)
productGroups.blurb: 36 lines: 3 Free, 33 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 13 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP) from South Korea, Malaysia, Poland, Taiwan and Türkiye carries antidumping duties.

productGroups.label: Carboxylic acids with extra oxygen function (citric, lactic, salicylic)
productGroups.blurb: 62 lines: 11 Free, 51 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 27 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Citric acid and citrates, sodium gluconate and 2,4-D carry antidumping or countervailing duties from several countries; MAPA and BMK glycidic acid are DEA List I chemicals.

productGroups.label: Phosphoric esters (TCPP, lactophosphates)
productGroups.blurb: 6 lines: 1 Free, 5 dutiable (most at 3.7%); 4 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Alkyl phosphate esters such as TCPP from China carry antidumping and countervailing duties.

productGroups.label: Esters of other inorganic acids (phosphites, carbonates)
productGroups.blurb: 14 lines: 1 Free, 13 dutiable (most at 3.7%); 11 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Several phosphite esters are Chemical Weapons Convention schedule 3 chemicals.

productGroups.label: Amines (methylamines, aniline, hexamethylenediamine)
productGroups.blurb: 76 lines: 14 Free, 62 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 27 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Methylamine and ethylamine are DEA List I chemicals; some amines are controlled substances or Chemical Weapons Convention chemicals.

productGroups.label: Amino alcohols, amino acids and their salts (lysine, glycine, MSG)
productGroups.blurb: 72 lines: 16 Free, 56 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 42 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Glycine, L-lysine and monosodium glutamate carry antidumping (and some countervailing) duties; six lines are drug ingredients on the Section 232 list.

productGroups.label: Quaternary ammonium salts (choline, lecithins)
productGroups.blurb: 7 lines: 1 Free, 6 dutiable (most at 6.2%); 6 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. A U.S. antidumping and countervailing duty investigation of choline salts from China is under way.

productGroups.label: Amides (acetaminophen, lidocaine, ureines)
productGroups.blurb: 47 lines: 12 Free, 35 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 25 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. APAA, a methamphetamine precursor, is a DEA List I chemical with its own statistical line.

productGroups.label: Imides and imines (saccharin, guanidines)
productGroups.blurb: 14 lines: 5 Free, 9 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 7 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Nitriles (acrylonitrile, adiponitrile)
productGroups.blurb: 22 lines: 8 Free, 14 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 4 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. APAAN and benzyl cyanide are DEA List I chemicals.

productGroups.label: Diazo, azo and azoxy compounds
productGroups.blurb: 8 lines: 2 Free, 6 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 2 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Hydrazine and hydroxylamine derivatives
productGroups.blurb: 5 lines: 1 Free, 4 dutiable (most at 3.7%); 3 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Other nitrogen compounds (isocyanates MDI, TDI)
productGroups.blurb: 18 lines: 2 Free, 16 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 8 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) from China carries an antidumping duty.

productGroups.label: Organo-sulfur compounds (methionine, thiocarbamates)
productGroups.blurb: 40 lines: 7 Free, 33 dutiable (most at 3.7%); 23 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Methionine from France, Japan and Spain carries antidumping duties; thiodiglycol is a Chemical Weapons Convention schedule 2 chemical.

productGroups.label: Other organo-inorganic compounds (glyphosate, organophosphorus, silanes)
productGroups.blurb: 46 lines: 2 Free, 44 dutiable (most at 3.7%); 39 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. HEDP from China carries antidumping and countervailing duties; methylphosphonates and related phosphorus compounds are Chemical Weapons Convention chemicals.

productGroups.label: Oxygen heterocyclics (THF, lactones, furfural, coumarin)
productGroups.blurb: 34 lines: 5 Free, 29 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 16 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Furfuryl and tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol from China carry antidumping duties; safrole, isosafrole, piperonal, MDP2P and GBL are DEA List I chemicals.

productGroups.label: Nitrogen heterocyclics (most drug APIs, melamine, pyridines)
productGroups.blurb: 128 lines: 34 Free, 94 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 66 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. The chapter's largest heading: 21 lines are drug ingredients on the Section 232 list, melamine, hexamine, chlorinated isocyanurates and tolyltriazole carry AD/CVD orders, and fentanyl and its precursors are DEA-controlled.

productGroups.label: Nucleic acids and other heterocyclics (APIs)
productGroups.blurb: 43 lines: 9 Free, 34 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 18 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Seven lines are drug ingredients on the Section 232 list; N-cyclohexylbenzothiazole-2-sulfenamide (CBS) from China is under an AD/CVD investigation.

productGroups.label: Sulfonamides
productGroups.blurb: 19 lines: 5 Free, 14 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 6 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Vitamins and provitamins
productGroups.blurb: 18 lines, all Free. All Free, exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties (U.S. note 52(b)) and on no China Section 301 list, so vitamins from China pay no extra tariff.

productGroups.label: Hormones and steroids (insulin, peptide hormones)
productGroups.blurb: 29 lines, all Free. All Free, but 16 lines are on the Section 232 list: patented hormones pay 100% (15% from the EU, Japan, Korea and Switzerland).

productGroups.label: Glycosides (rutin, stevioside)
productGroups.blurb: 2 lines: 0 Free, 2 dutiable (most at 1.5%); 2 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

productGroups.label: Alkaloids (caffeine, ephedrine, opiates, nicotine)
productGroups.blurb: 24 lines: 22 Free, 2 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 2 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Most lines are Free; ephedrine, pseudoephedrine and phenylpropanolamine are DEA List I chemicals, and opiates and cocaine are controlled substances.

productGroups.label: Chemically pure sugars (arabinose, ribose)
productGroups.blurb: 2 lines: 1 Free, 1 dutiable (most at 5.8%); 1 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix. D-arabinose from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

productGroups.label: Antibiotics
productGroups.blurb: 17 lines: 16 Free, 1 dutiable (most at 3.5%). Almost all Free and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties; six lines are on the Section 232 list.

productGroups.label: Other organic compounds
productGroups.blurb: 5 lines: 1 Free, 4 dutiable (most at 6.5%); 4 can enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix.

rateTable.note: Rates shown in grey are inherited from the parent heading. HTSUS states a duty once on the 8-digit line and leaves the 10-digit statistical lines blank; this table resolves each line to the rate that actually applies to it.

workedExamples.title: Polypeptide hormone API from Ireland
workedExamples.body: The base rate is **Free** and heading 2937 is on the U.S. note 52(b) list, so the 10% Section 301 duty on EU goods does not apply. The line is on the Section 232 list (U.S. note 40(c)): a **patented** ingredient — one covered by a valid U.S. patent and listed in FDA's Orange or Purple Book, or the API or key starting material for such a drug — pays **15% of its value in place of the base rate** (9903.04.62), so a $10M shipment owes **$1.5M**. A **generic** ingredient pays nothing extra (9903.04.67), and so does an inactive ingredient, which is not a "pharmaceutical article" (9903.04.69). Ireland shipped $56.30B of Chapter 29 hormones to the U.S. in 2025.

workedExamples.title: Generic antihistamine API from India
workedExamples.body: The line's base rate is **6.5%** and India pays the 2026 Section 301 duty as **+10%** (9903.05.44), so with no claims the generic API owes **16.5%** — $16,500 on $100,000. Two claims can take that to **$0**: the line is on U.S. note 52(e), so an ingredient for use in pharmaceutical applications is exempt from the Section 301 duty (9903.05.89), and if the drug is listed in the Pharmaceutical Appendix the base rate is **Free (K)**. Generics pay no Section 232 duty (9903.04.67); the same API sold for a patented drug would pay **100%**, because India has no reduced rate.

workedExamples.title: Citric acid from China
workedExamples.body: Base rate **6%**, plus **12.5%** for China under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31) and **25%** under Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03): **43.5%** in total, or $43,500 on a $100,000 shipment. On top of that come the **antidumping and countervailing duty** cash deposits under the 2009 orders on citric acid from China, which Commerce continued on May 29, 2026; they are set per exporter and are not in the tariff calculator. Citric acid used in pharmaceutical applications can be exempted from the 12.5% (note 52(e)), but not from List 3 or the AD/CVD orders.

workedExamples.title: Sorbitol from Canada
workedExamples.body: Base rate **4.9%**. Sorbitol is on the U.S. note 51(b)(3) list of the **Section 338** duty on Canadian goods (9903.03.14), which adds **50%** even when the goods qualify for USMCA. A USMCA-qualifying shipment therefore pays **50%** (the base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty are waived); a non-qualifying one pays **64.9%** (4.9% + 10% under 9903.05.29 + 50%).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Except where the context otherwise requires, the headings of this chapter apply only to: (a) separate chemically defined organic compounds, whether or not containing impurities; (b) mixtures of two or more isomers of the same organic compound (whether or not containing impurities), except mixtures of acyclic hydrocarbon isomers (other than stereoisomers), whether or not saturated (chapter 27); (c) the products of headings 2936 to 2939 or the sugar ethers, sugar acetals and sugar esters, and their salts, of heading 2940, or the products of heading 2941, whether or not chemically defined; (d) products mentioned in (a), (b) or (c) dissolved in water; (e) products mentioned in (a), (b) or (c) dissolved in other solvents provided that the solution constitutes a normal and necessary method of putting up these products adopted solely for reasons of safety or for transport and that the solvent does not render the product particularly suitable for specific use rather than for general use; (f) the products mentioned in (a) to (e) with an added stabilizer (including an anticaking agent) necessary for their preservation or transport; (g) the products mentioned in (a) to (f) with an added anti-dusting agent or a coloring or odoriferous substance or an emetic added to facilitate their identification or for safety reasons, provided that the additions do not render the product particularly suitable for specific use rather than for general use; (h) the following products, diluted to standard strengths, for the production of azo dyes: diazonium salts, couplers used for these salts and diazotizable amines and their salts.

**Note 2.** This chapter does not cover: (a) goods of heading 1504 or crude glycerol of heading 1520; (b) ethyl alcohol (heading 2207 or 2208); (c) methane or propane (heading 2711); (d) the compounds of carbon mentioned in note 2 to chapter 28; (e) immunological products of heading 3002; (f) urea (heading 3102 or 3105); (g) coloring matter of vegetable or animal origin (heading 3203), synthetic organic coloring matter, synthetic organic products of a kind used as fluorescent brightening agents or as luminophores (heading 3204) and dyes or other coloring matter put up in forms or packings for retail sale (heading 3212); (h) enzymes (heading 3507); (ij) metaldehyde, hexamethylenetetramine or similar substances put up in forms (for example, tablets, sticks or similar forms) for use as fuels, or liquid or liquefied-gas fuels in containers of a kind used for filling or refilling cigarette or similar lighters, of a capacity not exceeding 300 cm³ (heading 3606); (k) products put up as charges for fire extinguishers or put up in fire-extinguishing grenades, of heading 3813; ink removers put up in packings for retail sale, of heading 3824; or (l) optical elements, for example, of ethylenediamine tartrate (heading 9001).

**Note 3.** Goods which could be included in two or more of the headings of this chapter are to be classified in that one of those headings which occurs last in numerical order.

**Note 4.** In headings 2904 to 2906, 2908 to 2911 and 2913 to 2920, any reference to halogenated, sulfonated, nitrated or nitrosated derivatives includes a reference to compound derivatives, such as sulfohalogenated, nitrohalogenated, nitrosulfonated or nitrosulfohalogenated derivatives. Nitro or nitroso groups are not to be taken as "nitrogen-functions" for the purposes of heading 2929. For the purposes of headings 2911, 2912, 2914, 2918 and 2922, "oxygen function", the characteristic organic oxygen-containing group of those respective headings, is restricted to the oxygen-functions referred to in headings 2905 to 2920.

**Note 5.** (A) The esters of acid-function organic compounds of subchapters I to VII with organic compounds of these subchapters are to be classified with that compound which is classified in the heading placed last in numerical order in these subchapters. (B) Esters of ethyl alcohol with acid-function organic compounds of subchapters I to VII are to be classified in the same heading as the corresponding acid-function compounds. (C) Subject to note 1 to section VI and note 2 to chapter 28: (1) inorganic salts of organic compounds such as acid-, phenol- or enol-function compounds or organic bases, of subchapters I to X or heading 2942, are to be classified in the heading appropriate to the organic compound; (2) salts formed between organic compounds of subchapters I to X or heading 2942 are to be classified in the heading appropriate to the base or to the acid (including phenol- or enol-function compounds) from which they are formed, whichever occurs last in numerical order in the chapter; and (3) co-ordination compounds, other than products classifiable in subchapter XI or heading 2941, are to be classified in the heading which occurs last in numerical order in chapter 29, among those appropriate to the fragments formed by "cleaving" of all metal bonds, other than metal-carbon bonds. (D) Metal alcoholates are to be classified in the same heading as the corresponding alcohols except in the case of ethanol (heading 2905). (E) Halides of carboxylic acids are to be classified in the same heading as the corresponding acids.

**Note 6.** The compounds of headings 2930 and 2931 are organic compounds the molecules of which contain, in addition to atoms of hydrogen, oxygen or nitrogen, atoms of other nonmetals or of metals (such as sulfur, arsenic or lead) directly linked to carbon atoms. Heading 2930 (organo-sulfur compounds) and heading 2931 (other organo-inorganic compounds) do not include sulfonated or halogenated derivatives (including compound derivatives) which, apart from hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen, only have directly linked to carbon the atoms of sulfur or of a halogen which give them their nature of sulfonated or halogenated derivatives (or compound derivatives).

**Note 7.** Headings 2932, 2933 and 2934 do not include epoxides with a three-membered ring, ketone peroxides, cyclic polymers of aldehydes or of thioaldehydes, anhydrides of polybasic carboxylic acids, cyclic esters of polyhydric alcohols or phenols with polybasic acids, or imides of polybasic acids. These provisions apply only when the ring-position hetero-atoms are those resulting solely from the cyclizing function or functions here listed.

**Note 8.** For the purposes of heading 2937: (a) the term "hormones" includes hormone-releasing or hormone-stimulating factors, hormone inhibitors and hormone antagonists (antihormones); (b) the expression "used primarily as hormones" applies not only to hormone derivatives and structural analogues used primarily for their hormonal effect, but also to those derivatives and structural analogues used primarily as intermediates in the synthesis of products of this heading.

**Subheading Note 1.** Within any one heading of this chapter, derivatives of a chemical compound (or group of chemical compounds) are to be classified in the same subheading as that compound (or group of compounds) provided that they are not more specifically covered by any other subheading and that there is no residual subheading named "Other" in the series of subheadings concerned.

**Subheading Note 2.** Note 3 to chapter 29 does not apply to the subheadings of this chapter.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 29: Organic Chemicals — Tariff Updates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 29 Tariff Updates 2026 — Chemicals & API Tariffs: Section 232 Pharma, Section 301, China, AD/CVD | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for organic chemical imports since January 2025: the IEEPA duties (including China's fentanyl duty) and their end, the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs and their pharmaceutical exemptions, the Section 232 duty on patented drug ingredients, and new AD/CVD orders — with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares the **2025 Basic Edition** of the tariff schedule, in force at the start of 2025, with the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 29 base rate changed.** 1,185 of the 1,227 lines are identical; 42 are new statistical lines that split existing provisions at the same rate — DEA-listed drug precursors (MAPA, APAA, BMK and PMK glycidic acids, 4-AP and 1-boc-4-AP) and named drug ingredients such as diphenhydramine, phenylephrine, lorazepam, dexamethasone, atropine, doxycycline, vancomycin and clindamycin, most of them added in Revision 11 (July 1, 2026).

The extra duties changed several times. In 2025 the **IEEPA** duties reached Chapter 29: 10% then 20% (later 10%) on all goods of China under the fentanyl order, 25% (Canada 35%) on non-USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico, and the April 2025 reciprocal tariff on goods of other countries except the 508 lines on its exemption list, mostly drug ingredients, vitamins, hormones and antibiotics. All IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**; the Section 122 surcharge that replaced them used the same exemption list and expired on July 23, 2026.

What applies now: the **2026 Section 301 tariffs** on 60 economies (10% or 12.5%, from July 24, 2026) on 1,139 lines, with a pharmaceutical-use exemption for 702 of them; the 25% Section 301 tariff on **Brazil** (from July 22, 2026); the **China** Section 301 lists (25% and 7.5%), which USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 continue; the **Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceutical ingredients** on 72 lines (from July 31, 2026 for the 17 Annex III companies and September 29, 2026 for everyone else); the 50% **Section 338** duty on four Canadian sugar alcohols and sugars (from August 22, 2026); and Russia's 35% rate. New **antidumping and countervailing duty** orders on L-lysine, MDI, erythritol, hexamine, vanillin, 2,4-D, alkyl phosphate esters and melamine are listed below for reference; they are set company by company and are **not in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 29 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and on Brazil and their exemption lists, the 2018–2019 China Section 301 lists, the Section 232 pharmaceutical duty, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Russia rates under U.S. note 30 and the Section 232 aluminum derivative duty on Russian goods, plus the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chapter 29 products are listed as reference entries; they are not priced in the tariff calculator. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceuticals and their ingredients
inEffect.exemption: Covers only the 72 Chapter 29 lines in U.S. note 40(c) — drug ingredients in 2918–2942 such as polypeptide hormones (2937.19), insulin (2937.12), steroids, antibiotics and many "Drugs" lines — and only when the goods are an active ingredient or key starting material for a patented drug listed in FDA's Orange or Purple Book. Generic ingredients: no extra duty (9903.04.67). Inactive ingredients, excipients and chemicals not used for a drug: no Section 232 duty (9903.04.69). Other lower headings: onshoring plan 20% (9903.04.64), onshoring plus an MFN pricing agreement 0% (9903.04.65), listed specialty products from listed jurisdictions 0% (9903.04.66), U.S.-origin API made into dosage form abroad (9903.04.68), clinical trials and R&D (9903.04.70). Patented articles under 9903.04.60–9903.04.66 are excluded from the 2026 Section 301 duties (note 52(f)(8)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A patented API from India, China, Singapore or Canada pays 100% of its value in total — the 100% replaces the base rate, it is not added to it. The same chemical sold for a generic drug pays only the base rate and any Section 301 duty.

inEffect.country: EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein
inEffect.measure: Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceuticals (deal rate)
inEffect.exemption: Same scope as 9903.04.60. Generics pay nothing extra (9903.04.67). Specialty products (orphan drugs, plasma-derived, cell and gene therapies, ADCs and others Commerce listed on September 23, 2026) from these countries pay 0% (9903.04.66).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A patented polypeptide hormone API from Ireland (2937.19) pays 15% of its value in total; Ireland supplied $56.30B of Chapter 29 hormones in 2025.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceuticals (UK rate)
inEffect.exemption: Set at +10% by Proclamation 11020 and cut to +0% from July 31, 2026 under the U.S.–UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement; patented UK ingredients must still be entered under 9903.04.63.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A patented ingredient made in the UK pays only its base rate (and the 10% Section 301 duty on UK goods only if it is not entered under a Section 232 heading).

inEffect.country: 60 economies (incl. EU, China, India, Singapore, Switzerland, Japan, UK, Canada, Mexico, Brazil)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (EU 10%, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland 12.5% in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: 88 lines are exempt for every use (U.S. note 52(b), 9903.05.86): all of 2936 (vitamins), 2937 (hormones) and 2941 (antibiotics), most of 2939 (alkaloids), and 2915.29.30, 2918.29.75, 2926.90.30, 2930.20.10 and 2933.19.23. 702 more lines are exempt when the goods are for use in pharmaceutical applications, even if entered Free (K) (note 52(e), 9903.05.89). Patented drug ingredients entered under 9903.04.60–9903.04.66 are excluded (note 52(f)(8)); USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94); 4,7-dichloroquinoline (2933.49.08) from Ecuador is exempt (note 52(j)(12)). 437 lines have no exemption at all — mainly industrial hydrocarbons, solvents, monomers and intermediates. The duty applies also when an FTA, GSP or Free (K)/(L) rate is claimed (note 52(a)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian acetone or methanol for industrial use pays its base rate +10%; the same chemicals from China +12.5% on top of the China lists; from Germany or Ireland 10% in total. A vitamin or antibiotic pays none of it; an API on the note 52(e) list for a drug maker pays none of it once the use is declared.

inEffect.exemption: 89 lines are exempt (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) — the vitamins, hormones, antibiotics and alkaloids of note 52(b) plus five 2903.19 chlorinated solvents; 703 more when for pharmaceutical use (note 50(a)(v), 9903.05.06); patented drug ingredients under 9903.04.60–9903.04.66 are excluded. The 25% is added to the base rate and to the 12.5% that Brazil pays under 9903.05.27.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Brazilian industrial chemical at a 5.5% base rate pays 43% (5.5% + 12.5% + 25%).

inEffect.exemption: Not new: List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03) covers 773 Chapter 29 lines and 9903.88.04 eight more 2931.90.90 lines; List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15) covers 43 lines, including mannitol, sorbitol and glycerol. 403 lines are on no list — among them all vitamins (2936), hormones (2937) and antibiotics (2941) and most alkaloids. Two product exclusions run until November 9, 2026: sodium adipate (2917.12.50.00) and NBPT (2929.90.50.95) (9903.88.69). USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the actions continue during their four-year review. The China lists stack with the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.31). The IEEPA fentanyl duty (10%, then 20%, then 10%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese citric acid (base 6%) pays 43.5% (6% + 12.5% + 25%) before antidumping duties; Chinese vitamin C (Free, note 52(b)) pays nothing extra.

inEffect.measure: Section 338 duty (offsetting Canadian discrimination, motor vehicles action)
inEffect.exemption: Only four Chapter 29 provisions are on U.S. note 51(b)(3): mannitol (2905.43), sorbitol (2905.44), glycerol (2905.45) and D-arabinose (2940.00.20). The 50% applies also to USMCA-qualifying goods and on top of the base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty. D-ribose (2940.00.60) was on the list from August 22 until Proclamation 11065 removed it from September 15, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian sorbitol pays 50% with a USMCA claim and 64.9% without one.

inEffect.measure: Rates in lieu of column 2 (U.S. note 30) and Section 232 aluminum derivatives
inEffect.exemption: Russia pays the column 2 rates (often 15.4¢/kg plus 40–60% for Chapter 29); on 128 lines listed in note 30(b) the rate is 35% instead. Five fluorinated-hydrocarbon lines (2903.43.10, 2903.45.10, 2903.49.00, 2903.51.10, 2903.59.90) are on the Section 232 aluminum derivative list and pay a further 200% as products of Russia (9903.85.68). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on Russia (9903.05.66) applies on top.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian Chapter 29 chemicals face column 2 or 35% rates plus 12.5%: the U.S. imported $3.5M of them in 2025.

changes.title: No Chapter 29 base-rate changes
changes.detail: Every line that exists in both editions carries the same General rate in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; 42 lines are new statistical breakouts at the rate of the line they were split from.

changes.title: CBS rubber accelerator from China: preliminary countervailing duty
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found countervailable subsidies on N-cyclohexylbenzothiazole-2-sulfenamide (CBS, 2934.20) from China; the antidumping investigation opened June 2, 2026 is still under way. Cash deposits apply from the preliminary determination; final determinations are pending.

changes.title: China Section 301 lists continue during the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their July 6 and August 23, 2026 anniversaries. For Chapter 29 this keeps 25% on 781 lines (List 3) and 7.5% on 43 lines (List 4A).

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), with no exemption list for chemicals. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Methionine antidumping orders: Commerce sunset results
changes.detail: In expedited sunset reviews, Commerce found that revoking the 2021 antidumping orders on methionine (2930.40) from France, Japan and Spain would likely lead to continued dumping. The ITC is conducting full reviews; the orders stay in force meanwhile.

changes.title: Section 232 pharmaceutical duty extended to all companies
changes.detail: The interim 0% heading for companies not named in Annex III (9903.04.61) ended. Patented drug ingredients on the 72 Chapter 29 lines now pay 100% (9903.04.60), 15% from the EU, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland (9903.04.62) or 0% from the UK (9903.04.63) unless a lower heading applies.

changes.title: THAM (tromethamine) from China: preliminary countervailing duty
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found countervailable subsidies on tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane (2922.19) from China; the antidumping investigation opened May 18, 2026 is still under way.

changes.title: Specialty-drug 0% rate defined
changes.detail: Commerce named the categories (orphan drugs, plasma-derived therapies, cell and gene therapies, ADCs, nuclear medicines, fertility treatments, CBRN countermeasures, animal health) and the jurisdictions — including the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, the UK and India, but not China or Singapore — whose specialty products and their ingredients enter at 0% (9903.04.66). CBP added 9903.04.70 (0%) for clinical-trial and R&D use.

changes.title: Fatty acids from Indonesia and Malaysia: preliminary antidumping duties
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found dumping of certain fatty acids (scope includes 2915.70, 2915.90 and 2916.15) from Indonesia and Malaysia, after preliminary countervailing duty findings in July 2026. Final determinations are pending.

changes.title: Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on L-lysine from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued AD and CVD orders on L-lysine (2922.41) from China; importers post cash deposits at each exporter's rate.

changes.title: D-ribose removed from the Canada Section 338 list
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 narrowed the U.S. note 51(b)(3) list from September 15, 2026; D-ribose (2940.00.60) no longer pays the 50%, while mannitol, sorbitol, glycerol and D-arabinose still do.

changes.title: Citric acid from India and Canada: preliminary antidumping results
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found dumping of citric acid and citrate salts (2918.14, 2918.15) from India and none from Canada; in June it had preliminarily found countervailable subsidies for both. Final determinations and the ITC's final vote are pending.

changes.title: 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian mannitol, sorbitol, glycerol and sugars
changes.detail: Products of Canada on U.S. note 51(b)(3) pay +50% (9903.03.14), including USMCA-qualifying goods. In Chapter 29 that is 2905.43, 2905.44, 2905.45, 2940.00.20 and, until September 14, 2940.00.60. Proclamation 11056 moved the start from August 19 to August 22, 2026.

changes.title: Antidumping order on R-32 refrigerant from China continued
changes.detail: After the first five-year review, the antidumping order on difluoromethane (R-32, 2903.42) from China stays in force.

changes.title: Corrosion inhibitor orders on China continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the AD and CVD orders on tolyltriazole and benzotriazole (2933.99) from China.

changes.title: Section 232 pharmaceutical duty starts for the 17 Annex III companies; UK cut to 0%
changes.detail: Patented drug ingredients imported for the large drugmakers named in Annex III to Proclamation 11020 pay 100%, 15% for EU/Japanese/Korean/Swiss origin. The same day Commerce cut the UK rate (9903.04.63) from +10% to +0%. Generics pay nothing extra (9903.04.67).

changes.title: Antidumping order on acrylate monomers and oligomers from South Korea
changes.detail: Commerce issued an antidumping order on certain multifunctional acrylate and methacrylate monomers and oligomers (scope includes 2916.12 and 2916.14) from South Korea; Taiwan has been under AD and CVD orders since March 11, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies; pharmaceutical exemptions
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). 88 Chapter 29 lines are exempt under note 52(b) and 702 more when for pharmaceutical use (note 52(e)); patented drug ingredients under Section 232 are excluded.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazil
changes.detail: USTR imposed 25% on all products of Brazil (9903.05.01), on top of Brazil's 12.5% under 9903.05.27. 89 Chapter 29 lines are exempt (note 50(a)(ii)), more when for pharmaceutical use (note 50(a)(v)).

changes.title: 36 new statistical lines (Revision 11)
changes.detail: Revision 11 split 18 Chapter 29 provisions to track DEA-listed precursors (MAPA, APAA, BMK and PMK glycidic acids, 4-AP and 1-boc-4-AP) and named drug ingredients (diphenhydramine, phenylephrine, dexamethasone, atropine, doxycycline, tobramycin, vancomycin, clindamycin, rocuronium, tacrolimus, timolol, acetylcysteine), plus ethylene carbonate and dimethyl sulfide. Rates did not change.

changes.title: Antidumping order on MDI from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued an antidumping order on methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI, 2929.10) from China.

changes.title: MSG antidumping orders continued
changes.detail: The antidumping orders on monosodium glutamate (2922.42) from China and Indonesia stay in force after the second sunset review.

changes.title: Citric acid orders on China continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the 2009 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on citric acid and citrate salts (2918.14, 2918.15) from China after the third sunset review.

changes.title: Tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol order on China continued
changes.detail: The antidumping order on tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (2932.13) from China stays in force after the fourth sunset review.

changes.title: Section 232 duties on patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients proclaimed
changes.detail: Proclamation 11020 set 100% on patented drugs and their active ingredients and key starting materials (U.S. note 40(c) lists 72 Chapter 29 lines), 15% for the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Liechtenstein, 10% for the UK, 20% with an approved onshoring plan and 0% with onshoring plus an MFN pricing agreement. Generics, biosimilars and their ingredients are excluded.

changes.title: AD and CVD orders on erythritol from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on erythritol (2905.49) from China.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026, with the reciprocal tariff's product exemption list (9903.03.03): about 508 of the 1,227 Chapter 29 lines were exempt, mostly drug ingredients, vitamins, hormones and antibiotics.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the China fentanyl duty, the Canada and Mexico duties and the reciprocal tariff, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but no longer collected.

changes.title: Acetone antidumping orders continued
changes.detail: The antidumping orders on acetone (2914.11) from Belgium, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea and Spain stay in force after the first sunset review.
changes.countries: Belgium, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Spain

changes.title: Hexamine orders on Germany, India and Saudi Arabia
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping orders on hexamethylenetetramine (2933.69) from Germany, India and Saudi Arabia and a countervailing duty order on India; China has been under AD and CVD orders since September 11, 2025.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Five Russian fluorocarbon lines added to the Section 232 aluminum derivative list
changes.detail: Commerce added 120 provisions, including five Chapter 29 fluorinated-hydrocarbon lines, to the aluminum derivative list; as products of Russia they pay +200% (9903.85.68).

changes.title: Canada IEEPA duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on non-USMCA goods of Canada (9903.01.10) went from 25% to 35%. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: AD and CVD orders on vanillin from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on vanillin (2912.41) from China.

changes.title: AD and CVD orders on alkyl phosphate esters from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain alkyl phosphate esters such as TCPP (2919.90) from China.

changes.title: AD and CVD orders on 2,4-D from China and India
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid and its salts and esters from China and India.

changes.title: Antidumping orders on DOTP from four countries
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping orders on dioctyl terephthalate (2917.39) from Malaysia, Poland, Taiwan and Türkiye; South Korea has been under an order since 2017.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff; many drug ingredients exempt
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and higher country rates (9903.02.xx) on products of all countries except Canada and Mexico. About 508 of today's Chapter 29 lines were on the Annex II exemption list (9903.01.32); hydrocarbons, solvents and most industrial intermediates were not. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: USMCA goods exempted from the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties
changes.detail: From March 7, 2025, goods entered under USMCA no longer paid the IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico; non-USMCA Chapter 29 goods kept paying 25%.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%, with no chemical exemption
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on all products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) rose from +10% to +20%. Unlike the reciprocal tariff it had no exemption list, so every Chapter 29 chemical paid it, on top of the Section 301 lists.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty: +10% on all goods of China
changes.detail: Executive Order 14195, aimed at the synthetic opioid supply chain, imposed +10% on all products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20) from February 4, 2025.

changes.title: Additional duties on products of Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01), in force from March 4, 2025, including Chapter 29 chemicals. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Melamine orders on six countries
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping orders on melamine (2933.61) from Germany, Japan, the Netherlands and Trinidad and Tobago and countervailing duty orders on Germany, Qatar and Trinidad and Tobago; India followed with AD and CVD orders on April 9, 2025.
changes.countries: Germany, Japan, Netherlands, Trinidad and Tobago, Qatar, India

changes.title: Glycine orders continued
changes.detail: The antidumping orders on glycine (2922.49.43) from India, China, Japan and Thailand and the countervailing duty orders on India and China stay in force.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 29 organic chemicals were **$103.86B in 2025**, +46.2% on $71.06B in 2024. Almost all of the increase came from **Ireland**: $65.56B, up from $25.66B, and $56.30B of it in heading 2937 (hormones). Across all suppliers, subheading 2937.19 — polypeptide, protein and glycoprotein hormones other than insulin and somatotropin — rose from $16.43B to $57.79B. Without Ireland, imports were $38.30B, down from $45.40B.

**China** ($9.15B) ships a broad mix: nitrogen heterocyclics (2933), hormones, organo-inorganic compounds (2931) and vitamins (2936). **India** ($4.20B) and **Singapore** ($2.81B) mainly ship drug ingredients in 2933 and 2934. Imports from **Switzerland** fell to $2.18B from $4.59B and from **South Korea** to $1.12B from $2.48B. **Canada** is the largest source of hydrocarbons (2901). Comtrade figures do not say why a partner's trade moved, so we do not attribute these changes to tariffs.

These are 2025 figures: they include the IEEPA duties of 2025 but predate the Section 232 pharmaceutical duty and the 2026 Section 301 tariffs. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.h1: HTS Chapter 29: Organic Chemicals — Tariff Rates by Country

seo.title: Organic Chemical Tariff Rates by Country — Ireland, China, India, EU, Canada (HTS Ch. 29) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The total U.S. tariff on organic chemicals by country and product group: base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty, the China lists, the Section 232 duty on patented drug ingredients and the Canada Section 338 duty — for Ireland, China, India, Singapore, Germany, Canada, Switzerland, Japan and more.
keywords: us tariff on chemicals from india

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Where a group has several rates, the cell shows each total that some line pays; select it to see which lines carry which rate.

Three things decide most Chapter 29 totals. **Origin:** the 2026 Section 301 duty is 10% in place of the base rate for EU goods, 12.5% in place of it for Switzerland and Japan, +10% for India, the UK, Canada and Mexico and +12.5% for China, Singapore and Brazil — and China adds 25% or 7.5% under its older lists. **Product type** for the drug-ingredient lines on the Section 232 list: patented ingredients pay 100% (15% from the EU, Japan, Korea and Switzerland; 0% from the UK), generics nothing extra. **End use:** the matrix does **not** apply the pharmaceutical-use exemption from Section 301 (9903.05.89, 702 lines) or the Pharmaceutical Appendix (Free (K), 492 lines), because both depend on the importer's claim — an API for a drug maker often pays less than the cell shows. Antidumping and countervailing duties are not included.

rule.label: 2026 Section 301: 10% in place of the base rate (9903.05.39), so a non-exempt line pays 10% in total whatever its ad valorem base rate. 88 lines (vitamins, hormones, antibiotics, most alkaloids) are exempt from Section 301 (9903.05.86); 702 more when for pharmaceutical use (9903.05.89, not applied here). Patented drug ingredients on the 72 Section 232 lines pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.04.62); listed specialty products 0% (9903.04.66); generics nothing extra. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-12, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; SG for Singapore. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.

Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): 9903.05.89 (Section 301), 9903.05.06 (Section 301), 9903.88.69 (Section 301), 9903.04.64 (Section 232), 9903.04.65 (Section 232), 9903.04.68 (Section 232), 9903.04.70 (Section 232).
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

The pharmaceutical-use exemption from the Section 301 duties (9903.05.89 / 9903.05.06) and the Pharmaceutical Appendix (Free (K)) and dyes appendix (Free (L)) are not applied: they need the importer's claim. An API for a drug maker on a note 52(e) line pays no Section 301 duty, and a listed drug ingredient pays no base rate.
Section 232 cells show the patented, generic and specialty totals separately; "specialty" (0%) applies only to products Commerce has designated, from a listed jurisdiction.
The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied.

Antidumping and countervailing duties are not included: more than 25 Chapter 29 products carry orders (citric acid, glycine, MSG, L-lysine, MDI, melamine, hexamine, HFC refrigerants, acetone, vanillin, erythritol and others), at company-specific rates. Neither are the Superfund chemical excise tax or the ozone-depleting-chemical tax, which are paid to the IRS.

Entry rules still apply: DEA import declarations and permits for listed chemicals and controlled substances, TSCA certification, EPA allowances for HFCs and ozone-depleting substances, and FDA registration for drug ingredients.
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2, 20, 29, 30, 40, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 52(b) (9903.05.86) exempts 88 Chapter 29 lines (2936, 2937, 2941, most of 2939, and 2915.29.30, 2918.29.75, 2926.90.30, 2930.20.10, 2933.19.23) and note 52(e) (9903.05.89) 702 more when for pharmaceutical use; the Brazil lists 50(a)(ii) and 50(a)(v) cover 89 and 703 lines. Note 52(j)(12) exempts 4,7-dichloroquinoline (2933.49.08) from Ecuador. Note 40(c) lists 72 Chapter 29 lines for Section 232. Note 20: 773 lines on List 3 (20(f)), 8 under 20(g), 43 on List 4A (20(s)); exclusions in 20(vvv)(iii) for sodium adipate and NBPT run to November 9, 2026. Note 51(b)(3) lists four Chapter 29 provisions for Canada; note 30(b) lists 128 lines for Russia. The ended reciprocal tariff and Section 122 surcharge exempted about 508 lines (note 2(v)(iii)(a), 9903.03.03).
