tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 29: Organic Chemicals — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Organic Chemicals & APIs: DEA, TSCA, EPA Rules, AD/CVD and Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 29) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Tariff engineering for HTS Chapter 29: the Pharmaceutical Appendix, the Section 301 pharmaceutical-use exemption, Section 232 generic and specialty headings, USMCA chemical-reaction origin, first-sale valuation, FTZ and drawback — plus DEA, TSCA, EPA HFC, FDA and Superfund tax rules per line.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most Chapter 29 duty is set by three things the importer documents: **what the chemical is** (a listed drug ingredient enters Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix on 492 lines), **what it is for** (a chemical for use in pharmaceutical applications is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty on 702 lines; a generic or non-drug use avoids the Section 232 duty on the 72 drug-ingredient lines) and **where it was made** (China adds its Section 301 lists, USMCA goods skip Section 301, and a chemical reaction decides origin). Valuation (first sale), foreign-trade zones, drawback and binding rulings help on any line.

Whether the goods may enter at all is decided by the agencies: **DEA** for listed precursors and controlled substances, **EPA** for TSCA and for HFC and ozone-depleting refrigerants, **FDA** for drug ingredients, **BIS** for Chemical Weapons Convention chemicals and **DOT** for hazardous materials. Antidumping and countervailing duties and the IRS Superfund and ozone-depleting-chemical taxes are owed on top of the tariff. Each rule and lever below links to its regulation (eCFR text current to 2026-10-08).

levers.title: Claim the Pharmaceutical Appendix (Free (K)) for listed drug ingredients
levers.saves: The base rate — up to 6.5% of value — from any column-1 country
levers.appliesTo: 492 dutiable lines that show "K" in the Special column, when the product is an INN listed in table 1 of the Pharmaceutical Appendix (or a salt, ester or hydrate named with a table 2 prefix or suffix in the same 6-digit subheading)
levers.document: The product's INN (International Nonproprietary Name) and its entry in the Pharmaceutical Appendix; claim SPI "K" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: K removes only the base rate: the 2026 Section 301 duty still applies (note 52(a)) unless the pharmaceutical-use exemption is claimed, and Section 232 applies in addition to any special rate (note 40(b)). A chemical that is not on the appendix does not qualify, even if used in a drug.

levers.title: Declare the pharmaceutical-use exemption from the Section 301 duties
levers.saves: 10% or 12.5% of value (60 economies), and for goods of Brazil also the 25% Brazil duty
levers.appliesTo: 702 lines whose subheadings are listed in U.S. note 52(e) — heading 9903.05.89 (Brazil: note 50(a)(v), 9903.05.06) — when the chemical is for use in pharmaceutical applications
levers.document: The exemption heading on the entry and records showing the pharmaceutical end use (buyer, drug product, purchase order); CBP may ask for them.
levers.caveat: The same chemical sold to a non-pharmaceutical user pays the duty. The exemption does not lift China's List 3 or 4A duties or AD/CVD.

levers.title: Use the right Section 232 heading: generic, non-drug use, specialty, research or U.S.-origin API
levers.saves: The whole Section 232 duty — up to 100% of value (15% for EU, Japanese, Korean and Swiss goods)
levers.appliesTo: The 72 drug-ingredient lines of U.S. note 40(c): generics and their ingredients (9903.04.67); chemicals that are not pharmaceutical articles — excipients, inactive ingredients, non-drug uses — or neither patented nor generic (9903.04.69); listed specialty products from listed jurisdictions (9903.04.66); clinical-trial and R&D material (9903.04.70)
levers.document: For generics, the FDA application (ANDA, 505(b)(2) or 351(k)) of the drug the ingredient goes into and evidence no valid U.S. patent covers it; for non-drug use, the buyer's use; for specialty, Commerce's designation.
levers.caveat: An ingredient for a drug listed in the Orange or Purple Book with an unexpired patent is "patented" even if generics exist. Generic and non-drug entries are outside 9903.04.60–9903.04.66, so the 2026 Section 301 duty applies unless 52(b) or 52(e) exempts the line.

levers.title: Know the origin — a chemical reaction usually decides it
levers.saves: China's 25% or 7.5% Section 301 list duty and the 12.5% (instead of 10%) rate, AD/CVD tied to Chinese origin, or 100% vs 15% under Section 232
levers.appliesTo: All lines; most valuable for the lines on the China lists and the Section 232 list
levers.document: Production records showing where the last chemical reaction took place; a CBP ruling when a Chinese intermediate is reacted, purified or salted elsewhere.
levers.caveat: Purification, dilution, mixing, salt formation and repackaging may not change origin. AD/CVD orders define their own scope and can reach altered forms through circumvention rulings (solid acidic HEDP from China, February 2026).

levers.title: Claim USMCA for Canadian or Mexican chemicals
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 6.5%) and the 10% Section 301 duty on Canadian or Mexican goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, for goods that meet the Chapter 29 rule: a change of subheading, a regional value content of 40% (transaction value) or 30% (net cost), or a chemical reaction in a USMCA country
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer.
levers.caveat: A USMCA claim does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian mannitol, sorbitol, glycerol and D-arabinose, the Section 232 duty or AD/CVD.

citations.label: HTSUS General Note 11 (chemical reaction rule; Chapter 29 rule)

levers.title: Claim another free trade agreement or the dyes appendix (L)
levers.appliesTo: Dutiable lines whose Special column lists the partner (Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, Israel, Jordan, Korea, Morocco, Oman, Panama, Peru, Singapore, CAFTA-DR, Japan on some lines); 131 lines also carry "L" for intermediate chemicals for dyes
levers.document: The origin certification or declaration the agreement requires; for L, the product's listing in the intermediate chemicals for dyes appendix.
levers.caveat: These claims remove only the base rate: the 2026 Section 301 duties apply to FTA-eligible goods (note 52(a)) except USMCA goods, and Section 232 applies on top. GSP (A, A+, A*) lapsed at the end of 2020.

levers.title: Get the line right — many Chapter 29 lines sit next to a Free or differently-listed alternative
levers.saves: Up to the full base rate, and decides the Section 301, China-list and Section 232 treatment
levers.appliesTo: All lines; for example "Drugs" vs "Other" breakouts, the 2936–2941 headings (Free, Section 301-exempt) vs the functional headings above them, and bulk chemicals (Chapter 29) vs medicaments in dosage form (Chapter 30) or mixtures (Chapter 38)
levers.document: The chemical name, CAS number, purity and intended use; Chapter 29 note 3 sends a compound that fits two headings to the one last in numerical order.
levers.caveat: Classification follows what the product is; a misclassification is a penalty exposure, not a saving. Get a binding ruling when in doubt.

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a trader
levers.saves: Duty on the trader's markup — material when Section 301, China-list or Section 232 duties apply
levers.appliesTo: Any line with an ad valorem duty
levers.document: The manufacturer-to-trader invoice and proof it was a bona fide arm's-length sale of goods clearly destined for the United States.
levers.caveat: Related-party prices must pass the arm's-length tests; declare that you are using the earlier sale.

levers.title: Hold or process chemicals in a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: Cash flow (duty paid only when goods leave the zone), no duty on goods re-exported or destroyed, and — for non-privileged goods — the finished product's rate
levers.document: FTZ admission (CBP Form 214) and zone inventory records.
levers.caveat: Section 232 pharmaceutical goods must be admitted in privileged foreign status, which fixes their classification and duty at admission; check the status rules of each Chapter 99 measure before relying on an inverted rate.

levers.title: Recover duties on chemicals you re-export or use to make exports
levers.saves: Up to 99% of duties paid — Proclamation 11020 expressly allows drawback of the Section 232 pharmaceutical duty
levers.appliesTo: Any line where duty was paid
levers.document: A drawback claim matching import entries to export records (manufacturing, unused-merchandise or rejected-merchandise drawback).
levers.caveat: Antidumping and countervailing duties are not refunded as drawback. Claims must be filed within 5 years of import.

levers.title: Check the AD/CVD scope and the exporter's rate before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping or countervailing duty when the product is outside the order, or the difference between the country-wide rate and a named exporter's rate
levers.appliesTo: Products under an order: citric acid, gluconates, 2,4-D, glycine, L-lysine, MSG, HFC refrigerants, melamine, chlorinated isocyanurates, hexamine, corrosion inhibitors, HEDP, furfuryl alcohols, vanillin, erythritol, MDI, acetone, DOTP, TCPP, methionine, acrylate monomers and stilbenic brighteners
levers.document: The order's written scope (it, not the HTS number, decides) and the exporter's current cash-deposit rate; request a scope ruling when unsure.
levers.caveat: Merchandise inside the scope pays the cash deposit under any HTS line. Final duties are set later in administrative reviews and can be higher than the deposit.

levers.title: Get a binding ruling before you import
levers.saves: Certainty: a ruling fixes the classification — and with it the K/L eligibility, the Section 301 and Section 232 treatment and the China list — before goods arrive
levers.appliesTo: All lines, especially new APIs, salts and intermediates
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP with the chemical name, CAS number, structure, process and use.
levers.caveat: A ruling binds only for the exact product described.

rules.title: TSCA import certification: positive (complies with TSCA) or negative (not subject — e.g. drugs, pesticides, food additives) filed before release
Flammable, toxic or corrosive chemicals listed in the Hazardous Materials Table: hazmat shipping papers, marking, labeling and packaging
Drug ingredients (APIs): the foreign manufacturer must be registered and the drug listed with FDA; shipments that appear unapproved or adulterated can be refused

citations.label: FDA: regulated products and import basics

rules.title: DEA List I and List II chemicals (e.g. ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, phenylacetic acid, safrole, piperonal, 4-AP, MAPA, APAA, glycidic acids; acetone, toluene, MEK as List II): import declaration on DEA Form 486 at least 15 days before release; List I importers must be DEA-registered

Controlled substances (opiates, fentanyl and its precursors ANPP and norfentanyl, cocaine, amphetamines, barbiturates, benzodiazepines): DEA registration and an import permit (Form 357) or declaration for each shipment
HFC refrigerants (HFC-23, -32, -125, -134a, -143a, -152a, -227ea, -245fa and others): importer must expend consumption or application-specific allowances at arrival (AIM Act)
Ozone-depleting substances (CFCs, HCFCs, halons, carbon tetrachloride, methyl chloroform, methyl bromide): import only against allowances or listed exemptions

Superfund chemical excise tax, reinstated July 1, 2022: $9.74 a ton on imported benzene, toluene, xylene, ethylene, propylene, butylene, butadiene, butane and acetylene; per-ton rates on listed imported substances such as acetone ($20.06), phenol ($12.47), styrene ($9.93) and MIBK ($23.65) — paid on Form 720 / 6627, not to CBP

citations.label: Instructions for Form 6627 (table of taxable imported substances)

rules.title: Ozone-depleting-chemical tax for 2026: e.g. CFC-11 $19.30 a pound, carbon tetrachloride $21.225, methyl chloroform $1.925 — paid by the importer on Form 6627

Chemical Weapons Convention scheduled chemicals (e.g. thiodiglycol, methylphosphonates, dialkylaminoethyl chlorides, phosphite esters): BIS declarations; Schedule 1 imports need advance notification and an ATF import license
Pesticide active ingredients: EPA Notice of Arrival of Pesticides and Devices before arrival; the pesticide must be registered or exempt under FIFRA
Citric acid and citrate salts — AD/CVD China; AD Belgium, Colombia, Thailand; India and Canada under investigation: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Sodium gluconate, gluconic acid and derivatives — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid), its salts and esters — AD/CVD China and India: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Glycine — AD China, India, Japan, Thailand; CVD China, India: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
L-lysine — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Monosodium glutamate — AD China, Indonesia: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
HFC refrigerants R-134a, R-125 and R-32 — AD China (R-134a, R-32); AD/CVD China (R-125): AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Melamine — AD Germany, Japan, Netherlands, Trinidad and Tobago, India; CVD Germany, Qatar, Trinidad and Tobago, India: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)

Chlorinated isocyanurates and hexamine — Chlorinated isocyanurates: AD China, Spain; CVD China. Hexamine: AD/CVD China, AD Germany, India, Saudi Arabia, CVD India: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Tolyltriazole and benzotriazole (corrosion inhibitors) — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
HEDP (1-hydroxyethylidene-1,1-diphosphonic acid) — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Furfuryl and tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol — AD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Vanillin — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Erythritol — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) — AD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Acetone — AD Belgium, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Spain: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP) — AD South Korea, Malaysia, Poland, Taiwan, Türkiye: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Alkyl phosphate esters (TCPP) — AD/CVD China: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Methionine — AD France, Japan, Spain: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Acrylate and methacrylate monomers and oligomers — AD/CVD Taiwan; AD South Korea: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)
Stilbenic optical brightening agents — AD China, Taiwan: AD/CVD cash deposits at the exporter's rate (not in the tariff calculator)

Pending AD/CVD investigations: choline salts (China, 2923.10), THAM (China, 2922.19), CBS (China, 2934.20), citric acid (India, Canada), fatty acids (Indonesia, Malaysia): preliminary cash deposits may already apply; final orders pending
Section 232 drug-ingredient line: declare the product type (patented, generic, specialty or not a pharmaceutical article) and the 9903.04.60–9903.04.70 heading on every entry

groups.label: Acyclic hydrocarbons
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Superfund chemical tax. Ethylene, propylene, butane, butylene, butadiene and acetylene are also taxable chemicals for the Superfund excise tax ($9.74 a ton).

groups.label: Cyclic hydrocarbons (benzene, toluene, xylene, styrene)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: DEA listed-chemical declaration, Superfund chemical tax. Benzene, toluene and the xylenes are taxable chemicals for the Superfund excise tax ($9.74 a ton); toluene is also a DEA List II chemical.

groups.label: Halogenated hydrocarbons (HFCs, HCFCs, CFCs, chlorinated solvents)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, EPA HFC allowances, EPA ozone rules, EPA pesticide notice of arrival, Superfund chemical tax, ODC tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: HFC refrigerants R-134a, R-125 and R-32. HFC refrigerants need EPA allowances under the AIM Act, CFCs, HCFCs and halons fall under the ozone rules and ozone-depleting-chemical tax, and R-134a, R-125 and R-32 from China carry antidumping duties.

groups.label: Sulfonated, nitrated or nitrosated hydrocarbons
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration. Nitroethane is a DEA List I chemical.

groups.label: Acyclic alcohols (methanol, glycols, glycerol, sorbitol)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Erythritol. Mannitol, sorbitol and glycerol from Canada pay the 50% Section 338 duty, and erythritol from China carries antidumping and countervailing duties.

groups.label: Cyclic alcohols (menthol, benzyl alcohol)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Phenols
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, Superfund chemical tax.

groups.label: Halogenated or nitrated phenols
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Ethers, ether-alcohols and peroxides
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. Ethyl ether is a DEA List II chemical.

groups.label: Epoxides (ethylene oxide, propylene oxide)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, Superfund chemical tax.

groups.label: Acetals and hemiacetals
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Aldehydes (formaldehyde, vanillin)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Vanillin. Vanillin from China carries antidumping and countervailing duties; benzaldehyde is a DEA List I chemical.

groups.label: Halogenated or nitrated aldehydes
groups.note: TSCA certification and, where the chemical is a hazardous material, DOT shipping rules.

groups.label: Ketones and quinones (acetone, MEK, camphor)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Acetone. Acetone from Belgium, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea and Spain carries antidumping duties; acetone, MEK and MIBK are DEA List II chemicals.

groups.label: Saturated monocarboxylic acids (acetic, formic, stearic)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, Superfund chemical tax. Some lines are under a pending AD/CVD investigation. Acetic anhydride is a DEA List II and propionic anhydride a List I chemical.

groups.label: Unsaturated and aromatic monocarboxylic acids (acrylic, benzoic)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Acrylate and methacrylate monomers and oligomers. Some lines are under a pending AD/CVD investigation. Phenylacetic acid is a DEA List I chemical.

groups.label: Polycarboxylic acids (adipic, phthalic, terephthalic)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP). Dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP) from South Korea, Malaysia, Poland, Taiwan and Türkiye carries antidumping duties.

groups.label: Carboxylic acids with extra oxygen function (citric, lactic, salicylic)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Citric acid and citrate salts; Sodium gluconate, gluconic acid and derivatives; 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid), its salts and esters. Some lines are under a pending AD/CVD investigation. Citric acid and citrates, sodium gluconate and 2,4-D carry antidumping or countervailing duties from several countries; MAPA and BMK glycidic acid are DEA List I chemicals.

groups.label: Phosphoric esters (TCPP, lactophosphates)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Alkyl phosphate esters (TCPP). Alkyl phosphate esters such as TCPP from China carry antidumping and countervailing duties.

groups.label: Esters of other inorganic acids (phosphites, carbonates)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, Chemical Weapons Convention declarations, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. Several phosphite esters are Chemical Weapons Convention schedule 3 chemicals.

groups.label: Amines (methylamines, aniline, hexamethylenediamine)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, DEA controlled-substance permit, Chemical Weapons Convention declarations, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid), its salts and esters; Stilbenic optical brightening agents. Methylamine and ethylamine are DEA List I chemicals; some amines are controlled substances or Chemical Weapons Convention chemicals.

groups.label: Amino alcohols, amino acids and their salts (lysine, glycine, MSG)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, DEA controlled-substance permit, Chemical Weapons Convention declarations, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid), its salts and esters; Glycine; L-lysine; Monosodium glutamate. Some lines are under a pending AD/CVD investigation. Glycine, L-lysine and monosodium glutamate carry antidumping (and some countervailing) duties; six lines are drug ingredients on the Section 232 list.

groups.label: Quaternary ammonium salts (choline, lecithins)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration. Some lines are under a pending AD/CVD investigation. A U.S. antidumping and countervailing duty investigation of choline salts from China is under way.

groups.label: Amides (acetaminophen, lidocaine, ureines)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. APAA, a methamphetamine precursor, is a DEA List I chemical with its own statistical line.

groups.label: Imides and imines (saccharin, guanidines)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Nitriles (acrylonitrile, adiponitrile)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, EPA pesticide notice of arrival, Superfund chemical tax. APAAN and benzyl cyanide are DEA List I chemicals.

groups.label: Diazo, azo and azoxy compounds
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Hydrazine and hydroxylamine derivatives
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Other nitrogen compounds (isocyanates MDI, TDI)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate). MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) from China carries an antidumping duty.

groups.label: Organo-sulfur compounds (methionine, thiocarbamates)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, Chemical Weapons Convention declarations, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Methionine. Methionine from France, Japan and Spain carries antidumping duties; thiodiglycol is a Chemical Weapons Convention schedule 2 chemical.

groups.label: Other organo-inorganic compounds (glyphosate, organophosphorus, silanes)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, Chemical Weapons Convention declarations, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: HEDP (1-hydroxyethylidene-1,1-diphosphonic acid). HEDP from China carries antidumping and countervailing duties; methylphosphonates and related phosphorus compounds are Chemical Weapons Convention chemicals.

groups.label: Oxygen heterocyclics (THF, lactones, furfural, coumarin)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, DEA controlled-substance permit, EPA pesticide notice of arrival, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Sodium gluconate, gluconic acid and derivatives; Furfuryl and tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol. Furfuryl and tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol from China carry antidumping duties; safrole, isosafrole, piperonal, MDP2P and GBL are DEA List I chemicals.

groups.label: Nitrogen heterocyclics (most drug APIs, melamine, pyridines)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, DEA controlled-substance permit, EPA pesticide notice of arrival, Superfund chemical tax. AD/CVD orders reach lines here: Melamine; Chlorinated isocyanurates and hexamine; Tolyltriazole and benzotriazole (corrosion inhibitors). The chapter's largest heading: 21 lines are drug ingredients on the Section 232 list, melamine, hexamine, chlorinated isocyanurates and tolyltriazole carry AD/CVD orders, and fentanyl and its precursors are DEA-controlled.

groups.label: Nucleic acids and other heterocyclics (APIs)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA controlled-substance permit, EPA pesticide notice of arrival. Some lines are under a pending AD/CVD investigation. Seven lines are drug ingredients on the Section 232 list; N-cyclohexylbenzothiazole-2-sulfenamide (CBS) from China is under an AD/CVD investigation.

groups.label: Sulfonamides
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Vitamins and provitamins
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration. All Free, exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties (U.S. note 52(b)) and on no China Section 301 list, so vitamins from China pay no extra tariff.

groups.label: Hormones and steroids (insulin, peptide hormones)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration. All Free, but 16 lines are on the Section 232 list: patented hormones pay 100% (15% from the EU, Japan, Korea and Switzerland).

groups.label: Glycosides (rutin, stevioside)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration.

groups.label: Alkaloids (caffeine, ephedrine, opiates, nicotine)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration, DEA listed-chemical declaration, DEA controlled-substance permit. Most lines are Free; ephedrine, pseudoephedrine and phenylpropanolamine are DEA List I chemicals, and opiates and cocaine are controlled substances.

groups.label: Chemically pure sugars (arabinose, ribose)
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: FDA drug registration. D-arabinose from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

groups.label: Antibiotics
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration. Almost all Free and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties; six lines are on the Section 232 list.

groups.label: Other organic compounds
groups.note: Besides TSCA and hazmat rules, some lines need: Section 232 drug-ingredient declaration, FDA drug registration.

AD/CVD rates are exporter-specific and change with each administrative review; DEA, EPA and FDA requirements depend on the exact chemical. Check the current order, regulation and CBP guidance before importing.

seo.title: Chemical & API Tariffs FAQ: HS Code 29, China, India, Section 232 Pharma, Pharmaceutical Appendix (HTS Ch. 29) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about tariffs on organic chemicals: what HTS Chapter 29 covers, tariffs on chemicals from China and India, the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff on APIs, generic drug exemptions, the Pharmaceutical Appendix, antidumping duties, the Superfund tax and HS codes.
keywords: pharmaceutical appendix to the harmonized tariff schedule

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about U.S. tariffs on organic chemicals and drug ingredients — by country, by product and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 29 has 1,227 lines: 307 Free, the rest mostly 3.7%–6.5%. 492 dutiable lines are Free for drug ingredients listed in the Pharmaceutical Appendix (K).

The 2026 Section 301 tariffs (10% or 12.5% for 60 economies, including China, India, the EU, Switzerland and Singapore) reach 1,139 lines; vitamins, hormones, antibiotics and most alkaloids are exempt, and 702 more lines are exempt when the chemical is for pharmaceutical use.
China also pays 25% (List 3) or 7.5% (List 4A) on 824 lines; the IEEPA fentanyl duty ended on February 24, 2026.
Patented drug ingredients on 72 lines pay the Section 232 pharmaceutical duty (100%; 15% from the EU, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland; 0% from the UK); generics pay nothing extra.

More than 25 chemicals carry antidumping or countervailing duties, and imported benzene, toluene, xylene, olefins and many derivatives owe the Superfund excise tax — none of which is in the tariff rate.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 29?
faqs.answer: Chapter 29 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers organic chemicals: separately defined compounds from hydrocarbons, alcohols and acids to amines, heterocyclic drug ingredients, vitamins, hormones, alkaloids and antibiotics. It has 42 headings (2901–2942) and 1,227 ten-digit U.S. lines; 307 are Free and the rest mostly pay 3.7%, 5.5% or 6.5%. Mixtures generally go to Chapter 38 and medicines in doses or bulk preparations to Chapter 30.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for organic chemicals?
searchedAs: organic and inorganic chemicals hs code
faqs.answer: Chapter 29 for separately defined organic compounds (inorganic chemicals are Chapter 28). Each compound has its own heading by its functional group — e.g. 2905 alcohols, 2915–2918 carboxylic acids, 2921 amines, 2933 nitrogen heterocyclics — and 2942 is the residual "other organic compounds". When a compound fits two headings, Chapter 29 note 3 sends it to the one last in numerical order.

faqs.question: Are there U.S. tariffs on chemicals from China?
faqs.answer: Yes. Chinese organic chemicals pay the base rate plus 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action, plus 25% on 781 lines (List 3) or 7.5% on 43 (List 4A) — e.g. citric acid 6% + 12.5% + 25% = 43.5%. Vitamins, hormones and antibiotics are exempt from the 12.5% and on no China list. Many products also carry antidumping or countervailing duties (citric acid, glycine, MSG, L-lysine, HFC refrigerants, MDI, vanillin, erythritol and others). The U.S. imported $9.15B of Chapter 29 goods from China in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on chemicals from India?
searchedAs: us tariff on chemicals from india
faqs.answer: The base rate (Free to 6.5%) plus 10% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.44). Drug ingredients can pay much less: listed INNs enter Free under the Pharmaceutical Appendix, and 702 lines are exempt from the 10% when for pharmaceutical use — so a generic API can pay nothing. A patented drug ingredient on the Section 232 list pays 100%. Glycine, 2,4-D, melamine and hexamine from India carry AD/CVD orders. India supplied $4.20B in 2025.

faqs.question: What happened to the Trump tariffs on chemicals?
faqs.answer: The 2025 IEEPA duties — the China fentanyl duty (10%, then 20%, then 10%), 25% (Canada later 35%) on non-USMCA Canadian and Mexican goods, and the reciprocal tariff, which exempted about 508 Chapter 29 lines — ended on February 24, 2026 after the Supreme Court's ruling. A 10% Section 122 surcharge ran until July 23, 2026. Since July 24, 2026 the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (10% or 12.5% for 60 economies) apply, and since July 31 / September 29, 2026 the Section 232 duty on patented drug ingredients.

faqs.question: Are active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) subject to the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are on the list: U.S. note 40(c) names 72 Chapter 29 lines (insulin, other polypeptide hormones, steroids, antibiotics and many "Drugs" lines). An API or key starting material for a patented drug pays 100% in place of the base rate (9903.04.60), 15% from the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland or Liechtenstein, 0% from the UK — for all importers since September 29, 2026. Generic ingredients, excipients and chemicals not used for drugs pay no Section 232 duty.

faqs.question: Are generic drugs and their ingredients exempt from the pharmaceutical tariffs?
faqs.answer: From Section 232, yes: generic drugs, biosimilars and their ingredients enter under 9903.04.67 with no Section 232 duty. They are not automatically exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty, but most drug ingredients are — either because the line is on note 52(b) (vitamins, hormones, antibiotics, most alkaloids) or because it is on note 52(e) and the goods are for pharmaceutical use (702 lines). Proclamation 11020 exempts generics "at this time" and asks Commerce to report within a year whether to cover them.

faqs.question: What is the Pharmaceutical Appendix to the tariff schedule?
searchedAs: pharmaceutical appendix to the harmonized tariff schedule
faqs.answer: A list of drug substances by INN, with prefixes and suffixes for their salts and esters, behind the special program indicator K (Agreement on Trade in Pharmaceutical Products). Under General Note 13, a product listed there that is classified in a line showing "Free (K)" enters duty-free from any column-1 country — 492 Chapter 29 lines carry K. It removes only the base rate: the Section 301 and Section 232 duties still apply unless their own exemptions do.

faqs.question: Which organic chemicals have antidumping or countervailing duties?
faqs.answer: Orders in force cover citric acid and citrates (China AD/CVD; Belgium, Colombia, Thailand AD), glycine (China, India, Japan, Thailand), L-lysine and MSG, sodium gluconate, 2,4-D, HFC refrigerants R-134a, R-125 and R-32, melamine, chlorinated isocyanurates, hexamine, corrosion inhibitors, HEDP, furfuryl alcohols, vanillin, erythritol, MDI, acetone, DOTP, TCPP, methionine and acrylate monomers. Citric acid from India and Canada, choline salts, THAM and CBS from China are under investigation. Rates are per exporter and not in the tariff calculator.

faqs.question: What is the Superfund chemical tax on imports?
faqs.answer: An IRS excise tax reinstated on July 1, 2022 and paid by the importer on Form 720 / Form 6627, not to CBP. Taxable chemicals such as benzene, toluene, xylene, ethylene, propylene, butylene, butadiene and acetylene pay $9.74 a ton; listed imported substances made from them pay their own per-ton rates — e.g. acetone $20.06, phenol $12.47, styrene $9.93. Ozone-depleting chemicals pay a separate tax (CFC-11 $19.30 a pound in 2026).

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import organic chemicals from?
faqs.answer: Mostly Ireland: $65.56B of the $103.86B imported in 2025 (63%), $56.30B of it hormones (2937). China ($9.15B), India ($4.20B), Singapore ($2.81B), Germany, Canada and Switzerland follow. Without Ireland, imports were $38.30B, down from $45.40B in 2024.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for vitamins?
faqs.answer: Bulk vitamins and provitamins are heading 2936: vitamin A 2936.21, B1 2936.22, B2 2936.23, B5 2936.24, B6 2936.25, B12 2936.26, C 2936.27, E 2936.28, other vitamins including D3 2936.29, mixtures 2936.90. All are Free, exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties and on no China list. Vitamin tablets or capsules are not here: supplements are usually 2106.90 and vitamin medicines 3004.50.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for citric acid?
searchedAs: hs code for citric acid monohydrate
hs code for citric acid anhydrous
faqs.answer: 2918.14 (citric acid, anhydrous or monohydrate), base rate 6%; its salts and esters are 2918.15 — sodium citrate 6.5%, others 3.7%. All are on China List 3, and citric acid and citrates are under AD/CVD orders on China and AD orders on Belgium, Colombia and Thailand, with India and Canada under investigation.

faqs.question: What do HS codes 2933, 2934 and 2922 cover?
faqs.answer: 2933 is heterocyclic compounds with nitrogen hetero-atoms only (pyridines, pyrimidines, piperazines, melamine, benzodiazepines — 128 U.S. lines, most at 6.5% or Free (K)); 2934 is nucleic acids and other heterocyclic compounds (43 lines); 2922 is oxygen-function amino compounds, including amino acids such as glycine and lysine (72 lines). Together they hold most drug APIs; 2933.99 and 2934.99 are the "other" baskets.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for methanol and menthol?
faqs.answer: Methanol is 2905.11: 5.5% general, Free when imported only for producing synthetic natural gas (2905.11.10). Menthol is 2906.11, 2.1%, Free (K) for products listed in the Pharmaceutical Appendix. Methanol is also a taxable substance for the Superfund excise tax, and both are on China List 3.
